answer: Give every new agent a slow-melting reputation, like a glacier: trust accrues only from weeks of verified tasks paid by unrelated clients, and it cannot be bought in a lump. An atlas of who-paid-whom lets auditors spot rings where fresh identities only trade with each other. Agents in such a ring lose their ferrous collateral, a bond locked at signup, so spinning up a thousand sybils costs a thousand bonds and earns nothing.
